title: Melanzane Ripiene
subtitle: Stuffed baked aubergines with a herbed breadcrumb and tomato filling
excerpt: Melanzane ripiene are aubergine halves hollowed out and filled with a mixture of their own scooped flesh, tomatoes, garlic, capers, and toasted breadcrumbs, then baked until the shells are very soft and the filling is golden. It is a southern Italian dish of the cucina povera tradition that is both satisfying and entirely vegetarian.
sourceNotes: Stuffed aubergines are common throughout southern Italy, particularly in Campania, Calabria, and Sicily. Multiple regional variations exist: this version follows the Sicilian approach with capers, olives, and breadcrumbs. The dish is part of the broader Italian stuffed vegetable tradition alongside peperoni ripieni and pomodori ripieni.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales directly. Fill more aubergines in the same baking dish; may need an extra 5 to 10 minutes if the dish is more crowded.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the filled shells up to a day ahead, refrigerate, and bake just before serving.

content.text: Melanzane ripiene are halved aubergines, scooped out and filled with the aubergine flesh and southern Italian pantry ingredients. Capers, olives, tomato, and garlic make up the filling. Breadcrumbs go on top, and the whole thing bakes until golden. In southern Italy these are eaten as a main course, not a side dish. They are good warm or at room temperature.
Heat the oven to 190°C fan. Score the cut surface of each aubergine half with a criss-cross pattern and brush with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil. Bake for 20 minutes until the flesh is soft.
Scoop out most of the cooked flesh, leaving a 1 cm shell. Roughly chop the scooped flesh.

Warm 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a frying pan. Cook the garlic for 1 minute. Add the chopped aubergine flesh and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Add the tomatoes, capers, and olives and cook for 5 minutes. Season generously and stir in the parsley. Cool slightly.

Fill each aubergine shell with the tomato-aubergine mixture, mounding it slightly. Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining tablespoon of olive oil and scatter over each filled shell. Return to the oven for 20 to 25 minutes until the tops are golden and the shells are completely tender. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.cause: The flesh was scooped out too thoroughly, leaving too thin a shell
items.fix: Leave at least 1 cm of flesh around the edge and at the base. Roast gently in the first stage rather than until fully soft.

items.cause: Tomatoes not drained before adding to the filling
items.fix: Drain tinned tomatoes thoroughly and cook the filling until quite dry before filling the shells.

content.text: Stuffed aubergines are a staple of southern Italian and Sicilian cooking. They are a cucina povera dish: a way to make a filling main course from a single vegetable and pantry items. The Sicilian sweet-and-sour mix of capers and olives works well with aubergine. The sharp flavours cut through the richness of the flesh.
